messages:
Emily: heads up — thinking about adding a "runtime circuit_breaker" config to automatically pause or rollback routing/config changes if telemetry degrades. want opinions on signal selection + console UX.

Sam: high level — love it. main q: do we treat this as a feature-flag-level guard (per-flag) or a route-level policy (per-route/model)?

Emily: plan was per-config object that can target scope: route/model/global. flexible but default to route-level for safety.

Jia: signals: error-rate (4xx/5xx split), p95 latency, downstream_kv_miss spike, and request-volume drop (indicates client errors). windowing matters — use sliding 5m and 1h.

Nina: +1 on 5m and 1h. also need minimum sample threshold (e.g., >=100 reqs in window) to avoid noisy rollbacks on low traffic cohorts.

Kevin: agree on min-sample. also want a separate signal for content-quality regressions (per-eval prompt set), but that's future.

Emily: proto schema suggestion — simple JSON at control plane:

```
{"circuit_breaker": {
  "enabled": true,
  "scope": "route",   // route|model|global
  "signals": {
    "error_rate": {"threshold_pct": 5, "window_mins": 5},
    "p95_latency_ms": {"threshold_ms": 1200, "window_mins": 5}
  },
  "min_requests": 100,
  "actions": ["pause","notify"],
  "dry_run": true
}}
```

Sam: schema looks fine. a couple thoughts:
- threshold_pct should allow absolute count OR ratio? ratio fine.
- actions: need explicit rollback-to-last-known-good model/version for binary changes.
- we should record reason in audit log and attach a telemetry snapshot.

Jia: console UX: don't expose raw JSON by default. show a 3-step quick-config: pick scope -> pick signals (with suggested presets) -> pick action. advanced toggle for raw JSON.

Nina: presets idea is huge. devs usually pick default presets like "conservative" (1% errs, 500ms p95) vs "lenient" (5% errs, 2s p95). we should derive presets from historical baselines per-route.

Kevin: permissioning: changing circuit_breaker defaults should require approver role or at least 2-actor approval for global scope. route-level can be self-serve for owners.

Emily: +1. also want to tie to rollout system: when a config change is in-progress (cohorted rollout), the circuit_breaker should apply to that change specifically (so it can pause the rollout, not the entire route).

Sam: implementation debate: enforce at control plane (central) vs at edge/router layer. control plane easier to reason about and snapshot telemetry, but adds latency to decision loop. router-level gives faster pause but requires replication of rules.

Jia: hybrid: control plane computes decision and issues immediate cancel/pause to route proxies via a short-lived suppress rule. proxies also keep a local backoff if they detect the same signals to avoid control-plane RTT dependency.

Nina: metric instrumentation: we need an agreed set of metric names and tags so rule evaluation is deterministic. p95 should be computed on server-side and tagged by model+route+cohort.

ops-bot: alert (auto): "detect: route=chat/default error_rate 6.2% (5m) > cb.threshold 5% — pausing rollout id=rl-2026-004; dry_run=false" :warning:

Kevin: ops-bot sample is good. we must ensure alerts include runbook link and who was paged.

Emily: rollout tie-in details:
- circuit_breaker must be able to target rollout id
- pause should halt traffic shift and optionally rollback to pinned version
- dry_run mode logs decisions to allow false-positive tuning

Sam: telemetry gating: when creating cb config, suggest a "preview" that evaluates against historical data and reports expected firing rate before enabling.

Jia: can use existing replay infra to simulate detection on historical traces.

Nina: required UX features for console:
- preview modal with estimated firing probability
- enable toggle with approver flow for non-route scopes
- link to last 24h snapshot and comparison
- ability to mute notifications for a rollout

Kevin: API shape: POST /runtime/circuit_breakers -> returns id. GET /runtime/circuit_breakers/{id}/preview -> runs replay.

Emily: ownership: config metadata must include owner, escalation contacts, and required approvers. audit log entries include full diff, preview snapshot, and final decision.

Sam: tests: unit for rule evaluation logic, integration for control-plane -> proxy immediate apply, e2e for rollback flows with canary.

Jia: rollout plan: start with dry_run=true for 2 weeks, collect false positives, iterate presets. after confidence, enable dry_run=false for route-scoped only.

Nina: question: should we allow auto-escalation (if CB fires multiple times within 24h) to open a major incident? maybe toggleable.

Kevin: prefer an optional engagement escalation flag. keep default off.

Emily: action items:
- Emily: draft RFC with schema + preview UI mocks + replay plan (due EOD Thu)
- Jia: spike proxy suppress rule and local fallback (PR this week)
- Sam: add preview endpoint + replay hook
- Nina: define preset baselines per route
- Kevin: audit & approver flow design

Nina: lgtm. one more: add a telemetry tag to indicate which CB rule triggered (cb_id) so we can correlate.

Emily: good call.

Sam: thanks all — posting this to eng-runbooks and will start the RFC.

Kevin: :shipit:
